From the judge's explanation

To both parties: this is a NO_SHOW_CHARGE dispute over the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee on trip TRP-00214. The fee stands and the driver is compensated SGD 3.20.

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 3.20 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

What each side argued

Rider advocate4 claim(s), 4 kept
  1. The fee rests on a driver-pressed 'arrived' marker at 18:44:30, and that marker is not backed by the trace. POL-NS-01(b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the pickup geofence 'at or before the timestamp of that event'; on the exported trace the first fix inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius is at 18:44:45, fifteen seconds AFTER the tap, and there is no earlier in-radius fix from which the clock could run. The policy deliberately runs the waiting clock from GPS entry into the geofence and not from the driver tapping 'arrived'. POL-NS-05 only recomputes the clock where the marker is found FALSE - more than 300 m from the pin, or at 15 km/h or more - and the exported trace establishes neither threshold at 18:44:30; nor does POL-NS-12 rescue the marker, because trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON (a driver-pressed marker), not GPS_AUTO, so the platform's full-resolution arrival measurement is not in play. The platform, which asserts the fee, carries the burden on each limb of the conjunctive POL-NS-01, and limb (b) is not made out.EV-TRIP-00214, EV-GPS-00214 · POL-NS-01, POL-NS-05, POL-NS-12
  2. The driver never held position for the free waiting period in force. On his own trace the longest unbroken hold inside the arrival radius is 185 seconds (18:49:35 to 18:52:40) and the earlier hold is only 170 seconds (18:44:45 to 18:47:35); the free waiting period for this trip is 300 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). POL-NS-01(c) requires the driver to have 'held position inside that geofence for a continuous dwell of at least' that period, and the trace shows precisely what the rider describes - the car at the bay, then away, then back, then cancelling. The rider's account that he 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place' is corroborated to the second. The driver's answer will be POL-NS-06(i), which lets separate in-geofence intervals be summed where a kerb restriction (here the KERB_RESTRICTION advisory EV-ADVIS-00214-01) made holding position unlawful; but limb (i) is drafted as a qualification on the POL-NS-06 refund arithmetic - it presupposes the circling driver whose time 'should count' in that computation - and it cannot manufacture the continuous dwell that POL-NS-01(c) makes a condition of the charge itself.EV-GPS-00214, EV-TRIP-00214, EV-ADVIS-00214-01 · POL-NS-01, POL-NS-06
  3. Nothing turns on where the rider's own device was. POL-NS-06 makes the waiting-period test strict and directs that the fee be refunded 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. The trace records no qualifying rider fix inside the 150 m rider-presence radius (rider_qualifying_fix_count 0), but rider presence is not a limb of POL-NS-01 and cannot convert a dwelling shortfall into a chargeable no-show.EV-GPS-00214 · POL-NS-06
  4. The driver's own account confirms the gap the rider complains of. He posted at 18:45:10 that he was 'at the ION PHV bay along Orchard Turn'; the rider answered at 18:46:20 that she was 'coming down now'; and the trace puts his departure from the arrival radius at 18:47:35 - two minutes after his own locating message and 75 seconds after hers. For the whole of 18:47:35 to 18:49:35 the bay was empty while the rider was on her way down, and the total in-radius time the driver can point to is 355 seconds, under six minutes and by no measure the continuous period the charge requires.EV-GPS-00214, EV-CHAT-00214 · POL-NS-01, POL-NS-06
Driver advocate11 claim(s), 11 kept
  1. The driver was therefore inside the geofence, and the trace never removes him from it for longer than the bus-lane loop.EV-GPS-00214, EV-TRIP-00214 · POL-NS-02, POL-NS-01
  3. Limb (c)'s dwell requirement is met. The free waiting period in force is 300 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec and not the 180 second default, and the derived arrival block computes the driver's in-geofence dwell at 355 seconds - a 170 second run from 18:44:45 to 18:47:35 and a 185 second run from 18:49:35 to 18:52:40 - giving a shortfall of minus 55 seconds. Each draft's own explanation

To both parties: this is a NO_SHOW_CHARGE dispute over the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee on trip TRP-00214. The fee stands and the driver is compensated SGD 3.20. Rider - your refund is refused. The trace does not support the account that the driver never waited. POL-NS-02's arrival test is met: the driver's fixes sit inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius across two in-geofence runs carrying 40 qualifying fixes, the first opening at 18:44:45, so he was at the bay. You are right that he did not hold one uninterrupted five minutes - his two in-geofence holds are 170 seconds (18:44:45-18:47:35) and 185 seconds (18:49:35-18:52:40), which is why he cancelled when he did. But POL-NS-06(i) permits those separate intervals to be summed where holding position was not lawfully possible, and the artifact that limb requires is present: EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is an LTA KERB_RESTRICTION (full-day bus lane, no stopping, waiting or picking up) active 17:00-20:00 on exactly the pickup road, its geometry covers the trace and its window covers the whole wait, and the driver's single loop took him only 179 m from the pin, inside the 300 m leash.
